title: Swing Excess Line Corrections — Commercial Natural Gas Supply
content:
A swing excess correction on a Commercial Natural Gas Supply agreement is worked on the agreement's most recently posted swing excess charge line. The over-billed amount on that line is returned as one rebill credit, tied to the line through its source bill line reference and dated on the correction date.

## Scope

- **Disputing the line.** A business that asks for the line to be put right once it has been pointed out to it is disputing that line.
- **Agreements covered.** This correction covers an agreement whose plan has no portfolio bandwidth, or an agreement that is the business's only commercial gas agreement on a plan with portfolio bandwidth. Where the business has two or more agreements on plans with portfolio bandwidth, the portfolio measure decides the swing and the line is outside this correction.

| The business's commercial gas agreements | Is the swing excess line within this correction? |
|---|---|
| The agreement's plan has no portfolio bandwidth | Yes |
| The agreement is the business's only agreement on a plan with portfolio bandwidth | Yes |
| The business has two or more agreements on plans with portfolio bandwidth, this one among them | No; the portfolio measure decides the swing |

## Booking the rebill credit: `post_bizgas_swing_rebill_d99acf60`

**What it does.** `post_bizgas_swing_rebill_d99acf60` posts a rebill credit that returns money over-billed on one Beacon Ridge Commercial Gas swing excess bill line. One call adds one rebill credit line to the commercial gas agreement's billing ledger, tied to the corrected swing excess line, dated today and carried as a negative amount. The business sees the credit against that line on its next utility bill, and the agreement's net billed charges fall by the credited amount. The credit is booked exactly as given.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool. The care agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool`, giving the tool name `post_bizgas_swing_rebill_d99acf60`, and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`, passing the parameters below.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `bizgas_agreement_id` | The commercial gas agreement number of the site whose swing excess line is corrected, as shown on the agreement record returned by the commercial gas agreement lookup | Identifier, text |
| `source_billing_id` | The reference number of the swing excess bill line being corrected, as shown on that line in the commercial gas bill line lookup | Identifier, text |
| `billing_period_start` | The first day of the billing cycle of the corrected line, exactly as it appears on that line | YYYY-MM-DD, no time zone |
| `rebill_amount_usd` | The amount being returned on the line | A positive number of US dollars rounded half up to 2 decimal places; it is booked on the ledger in US dollars to 2 decimal places, signed, as a negative credit |

**Return.** A text rendering of a dictionary with the keys `status` (the literal "posted" when the credit was booked), `bizgas_billing_id` (the reference number of the new rebill credit line), `source_billing_id` (the corrected line's reference number), `amount_usd` (the signed credit booked, a negative number with 2 decimal places) and `posted_date` (today's date, YYYY-MM-DD).

## Illustration of a call (hypothetical values)

Unlocking `post_bizgas_swing_rebill_d99acf60` and calling it with `bizgas_agreement_id` "BG-AGR-1001", `source_billing_id` "BG-LINE-5530", `billing_period_start` "2025-01-14" and `rebill_amount_usd` 18.40 returns a status of "posted", a new line reference, the same source line reference, an `amount_usd` of -18.40 and today's date as `posted_date`.
